title: Daily routine
goal: Describe your routine from getting up to going to bed, and place events in time with *keur*, *geus*, *rék* and *can*.
bekal: four time markers that replace an entire tense system

dialogs.title: Paguneman — A day in Rani's life
dialogs.intro: Sari is curious how Rani spends her working day. This conversation packs every Sundanese time marker onto one page.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.id: What time do you usually get up?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Tabuh lima. Sanggeus solat subuh, kuring sok olahraga saeutik.
lines.id: Five. After the dawn prayer I like to do a bit of exercise.
lines.literal: hour five. after prayer dawn, I like exercise a-little.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.text: Wah, rajin. Ari kuring mah tara hudang saméméh tabuh genep.
lines.id: Wow, how disciplined. Me, I never get up before six.
lines.literal: wow, diligent. as-for I [mah] never get-up before hour six.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Terus mandi, dahar, tuluy indit ka kantor tabuh tujuh.
lines.id: Then I shower, eat, and leave for the office at seven.
lines.literal: then bathe, eat, then go to office hour seven.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.id: How do you get to the office?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Angkot. Kadang ojég lamun geus telat.
lines.id: Angkot. Sometimes an ojek if I'm running late.
lines.literal: angkot. sometimes ojek if already late.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.id: What are you doing now? Haven't you left yet?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Can. Keur ngadagoan hujan eureun heula.
lines.id: Not yet. I'm waiting for the rain to stop first.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.id: What time do you usually get home?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Tabuh lima soré. Tapi mindeng nepi ka imah tabuh tujuh, macét.
lines.id: Five in the afternoon. But I often only get home at seven, traffic.
lines.literal: hour five afternoon. but often reach to house hour seven, jammed.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.id: What do you like to do in the evening?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Ngadéngékeun musik, maca, kadang diajar basa Sunda.
lines.id: Listen to music, read, sometimes study Sundanese.
lines.literal: listen music, read, sometimes study language Sundanese.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.id: What time do you go to bed?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Sabenerna rék saré tabuh sapuluh, tapi sok kabablasan.
lines.id: I mean to sleep at ten, but I often stay up way too late.
lines.literal: actually will sleep hour ten, but like overshoot.

notes: **Tuluy** = then, next (loma); lemes **teras**. Different from **terus**, "straight on, right away." In conversation the two are often used interchangeably.
**Saméméh** = before (loma); lemes **sateuacan**. Its partner is **sanggeus** = after (loma); lemes **saatos**.
**Mindeng** = often (loma); lemes **sering**. Together with **sok** (usually, tend to) and **tara** (never), these make up the Sundanese frequency system.
**Kadang / kadang-kadang** = sometimes (the same word as in Indonesian). The more Sundanese choice: **sakapeung**.

**Kabablasan** = to overshoot, go too far. The prefix *ka-* plus the ending *-an* again, marking something that happens by accident. Same pattern: *kabeurangan* (to oversleep), *kahujanan* (to get caught in the rain), *kalaparan* (to go hungry).
**Sabenerna** = actually. From *bener* (true, right). The lemes form is *saleresna*, from *leres*.

grammars.title: Four time markers
body: Sundanese never changes the verb to show time: no "eat / ate / eaten." The whole job is done by four little words placed **before** the verb.

head: Loma
Lemes
English
Example
rows: *Tacan ka ditu.* — I've never been there.
*Tara dahar isuk.* — I never have breakfast.
*Sok dahar di dinya.* — I usually eat there.

after: ⚠️ The lemes form **tos** is short for *parantos* and you'll hear it far more often. *Tos tuang?* = have you eaten? Formal writing uses *parantos*; conversation almost always *tos*.

Watch the difference between **can** and **tacan**: *can* means not yet (but it will happen); *tacan* means never, not even once. *Kuring can dahar* = I haven't eaten yet (but I will). *Kuring tacan ka Ciwidey* = I've never been to Ciwidey.
The difference between **tara** and **teu**: *teu* negates a single event; *tara* negates a habit. *Manéhna teu datang* = he didn't come (this time). *Manéhna tara datang* = he never comes.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Lalajo** = to watch (loma); lemes **ningali**. It's a typically Sundanese word, not found in Indonesian: *lalajo bal* = to watch soccer, *lalajo pilem* = to watch a movie.

blocks.title: Putting activities in order
items: **terus / tuluy / teras** — then: *Terus dahar.* — Then eat.
**sanggeus / saatos** — after: *Sanggeus dahar, indit.* — After eating, leave.
**saméméh / sateuacan** — before: *Saméméh saré, maca.* — Before sleeping, read.
**bari** — while: *Dahar bari lalajo.* — Eat while watching.
**sabot / basa** — when: *Basa keur dahar, hujan.* — While (we were) eating, it rained.

blocks.text: To say what you usually do, combine a frequency word with a time expression. Word order is free, but the most natural place for the time expression is at the start or the end.

blocks.title: Asking about activities
items: **Ayeuna keur naon?** — What are you doing now?
**Biasana hudang tabuh sabaraha?** — What time do you usually get up?
**Badé naon engké?** — What are you going to do later?
**Kamari ka mana waé?** — Where did you go yesterday?
**Peutingna sok naon?** — What do you usually do in the evening?
**Unggal poé kitu?** — Like that every day?

blocks.text: Describing your day is the best A1 practice there is: the vocabulary repeats and the sentences are simple. Try writing a paragraph about your own day using the four time markers and three frequency words.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right time marker: keur, geus, rék or can.

I usually get up at five.
